newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong denies former immigration chief spied.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong denies former immigration chief spied.

text.p: Hong Kong's top civil servant on Wednesday denied that former immigration chief Laurence Leung was a Chinese spy.
"There is no evidence and no reason to suppose that Mr Leung is or was a Chinese agent," Chief Secretary Anson Chan told a panel probing the case.
A Legislative Council panel of inquiry, equivalent to a parliamentary inquiry, has pressured the government to release details of the case.
The administration originally said Leung had quit for personal reasons last July but changed its story last week and accused him of serious lapses in personal integrity.
Chan said there was no evidence that Leung had passed on confidential details about Hong Kong residents seeking British passports under a special scheme or on individuals seeking asylum in Hong Kong.

"There is no evidence and no reason to believe that the list of (British Nationality scheme) beneficiaries has been compromised. In any case, Mr Leung, as Director of Immigration, did not personally hold such a list."
"There is no evidence he has passed on information on asylum seekers to an unauthorised party. He did not hold such information, and there's no record of his seeking to acquire it."
